answer: One concrete defense is making identity costly and slow. Each new agent must post a time-locked bond before it can earn, so spawning a thousand sybils means locking a thousand bonds. Reputation then accrues only through witnessed work, like crossing a sable tundra on foot with no shortcuts. Every attestation is co-signed by random peers and published to a shared beacon others verify, so forged history is caught early. The attacker cost scales linearly with each fake agent while honest yield does not, making floods unprofitable.
